.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Benign weather continues through the remainder of October
  with near to above normal temperatures expected. 
 
- 2) Precipitation chances return in early November.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Benign weather continues through the remainder 
of October with near to above normal temperatures expected. 

A weak cold front will stall to the south and east this
afternoon. By Wednesday morning, the same front will retreat 
back to the north as a warm front. Another large area of high 
pressure will build to the north Thursday through Saturday. As a
result, expect passing high clouds and a series of wind shifts 
with each of the frontal passages. Winds will remain light out 
of the north and northwest this afternoon. Winds will change to
the south and southwest late Wednesday through Friday. This 
will yield seasonable to above normal temperatures for the 
remainder of the workweek. Highs will generally range from the 
mid 60s and low 70s though Wednesday with low to mid 70s 
Thursday and mid to upper 70s Friday. This is thanks to the 
position of the high to the north leading to increased southeast
to southwest winds across the region. Overnight lows will 
remain mild as well in the mid 40s and low 50s.

There is the potential for some low clouds, fog, or even a
little drizzle during the late night into morning hours each of
the next few days as onshore flow develops.

Otherwise, dry conditions will continue through Saturday, 
although this will be a day of transition as the pattern begins 
to loosen. Upper-level ridging will buckle with an incoming 
trough from the Midwest region. This trough will ultimately 
bring an end to the dry conditions with increasing cloud cover 
and precipitation chances heading into the first few days of 
November. Despite the increased cloud cover, expect highs 
Saturday back in the upper 60s and low 70s. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Precipitation chances return in early November.

Upper-level ridging overhead breaks down into zonal flow by 
Sunday. Conditions likely start to become cloudier by the second
half of the weekend as troughing develops over the Ohio River 
Valley before heading east Sunday into Monday. This will bring
the first chances for precipitation over the Mid-Atlantic in 
over a week, although overall breadth and total rainfall from 
this system remain uncertain at this time.

Temperatures likely drop back to the low 70s over the weekend 
in the wake of another weak (dry) front. With overnight lows 
generally remaining in the 40s and 50s, this ranges somewhat 
above normal for the beginning of November. Looking ahead, model
guidance hints at a second, potentially more potent upper-level
trough approaching the area that could bring additional chances
for precipitation by the middle of next week.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected through tonight. Winds 
will remain light out of the north to northeast. Light onshore
flow could lead to some patchy low clouds/fog in outlying areas
late tonight.

Winds will shift to the southeast Wednesday ahead of a warm 
frontal boundary. This will lead to the potential for low 
clouds and fog, especially at CHO and MRB given the marine 
influence/increased surface moisture banking along the eastern 
side of the Blue Ridge mountains and up the Potomac River Valley.
Confidence in this is low, although hi-res models have shown 
some consistency in recent cycles. Aside from early morning low
clouds and/or fog, VFR conditions are expected Wednesday night 
through Saturday as high pressure builds along the coast. Winds 
will turn south to southwesterly Thursday before becoming 
easterly Saturday. The next chance for rain showers occurs 
Sunday with an incoming cold front, but uncertainty remains high
at this time.

&&

.MARINE...
Light northeast to east winds expected through tonight.

Winds become southeasterly Wednesday before turning southerly 
Thursday. Some channeling is possible at times, though overall 
gradients look weak. Winds stay below SCA thresholds through the
end of the month. Southerly winds shift westerly on Friday, 
then northeasterly on Saturday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Light onshore flow Wednesday into Thursday may push sensitive 
shoreline close to minor flood stage. Areas most at risk for
reaching minor tidal flood thresholds would be places like 
Annapolis and Alexandria mainly during the evening tide cycles 
(which are astronomically higher).
